title: Policy 'troubles' judge: Recommends two officers be sent to top priority calls
article: The city's police department should review its staffing and dispatch policies for top priority calls, says a Calgary judge who was "troubled" only one officer was sent to an armed robbery that turned into a fatal hostage-taking.
Provincial court Judge Heather Lamoureux said although there is no way of knowing if two officers could have defused the situation, the department should examine its policies.
Lamoureux's recommendations were forwarded to the Alberta Minister of Justice and the Attorney General under the Fatality Inquiries Act.
Lamoureux presided over a fatality inquiry into the death of 34- year-old Arthur George Provencal.

Provencal, who was on parole at the time of the incident, was shot between the eyes by Calgary police Const. Julien Gagne as he held a knife to the throat of a Shoppers Drug Mart employee during a bungled robbery Dec. 23, 2000.
"The unanswered question is whether the outcome might have been different if two police officers had simultaneously attended at the scene," Lamoureux wrote in her report.

Gagne arrived at the drugstore to find Provencal demanding a lethal dose of drugs from employee Ernie Plaxton and looking to die at the hands of a police officer -- a phenomenon known as suicide by cop.
Gagne gave Provencal two warnings to drop his weapon before firing a single shot from his 40-calibre Glock semi-automatic weapon.
Lamoureux's report to the government expressed concern that on the night of the shooting a supervisor in the downtown district had permitted four officers to go home early.
The Calgary Police Service would not comment directly on the report's recommendations, but promises that it will review all of Lamoureux's suggestions.

During the inquiry, Calgary police deputy chief Rick Hanson said although two officers may have been beneficial in this instance, policy should not be changed to require two officers per car because 84 per cent of the 250,000 annual calls made to the department require only one officer.
